firstLetter.T: Source (transformer / generator) has a point directly connected to earth (terre).
firstLetter.I: Source is isolated from earth, or earthed only through a high impedance.

secondLetter.N: Exposed-conductive-parts of the installation are connected to the earthed point of the source (typically the transformer star point / neutral).
secondLetter.T: Exposed-conductive-parts are connected to a local earth electrode independent of the source earth.

thirdLetter.S: Protective earth (PE) and neutral (N) are separate conductors throughout.
thirdLetter.C: PE and N are combined in a single PEN conductor.
thirdLetter.C-S: PEN on the supply, split into separate PE and N at the origin of the installation (PME / MEN / MGN).

systems.name: TN-S
systems.conductors: PE and N separate from the source
systems.primaryProtection: overcurrent device; RCD additional for sockets / EV
evNotes: Preferred TN arrangement for EV charging: dedicated PE, no PEN on the EV circuit.
IEC 60364-7-722: a circuit supplying a connecting point shall not include a PEN conductor.
typicalRegions: Older UK urban (CNE/SNE split at substation)

systems.name: TN-C
systems.primaryProtection: overcurrent; RCD cannot be used on PEN
systems.openPenRisk: high — a broken PEN raises all bonded metalwork to dangerous potential
evNotes: Not acceptable for the EV charging circuit. PEN must be split (TN-C-S) and PE run separately to the EVSE.
RCDs required by IEC 60364-7-722 cannot operate correctly on a PEN conductor.
typicalRegions: Legacy LV distribution in some countries
Not used as a final-circuit arrangement for EVSE

systems.name: TN-C-S
systems.fullName: Terre Neutral — Combined then Separate (PME / MEN / MGN)
systems.installationEarth: PEN split to PE + N at origin
systems.conductors: PEN on the utility side; PE and N separate after the main earthing terminal
systems.openPenRisk: significant for outdoor EV charging — vehicle body can rise to line potential if PEN is lost
evNotes: Most common worldwide residential earthing system (UK PME, AU/NZ MEN, North American multi-grounded neutral).

UK BS 7671 722.411.4.1: PME shall not earth an outdoor charging point unless additional measures are used (earth electrode, open-PEN disconnection ≤ 70 V, electrical separation, or proven load balance).
EV circuit itself must still be TN-S from the origin (no PEN to the wallbox).

systems.name: TT
systems.installationEarth: local electrode only — no metallic PE from utility
systems.conductors: N from utility; PE from local rod / foundation earth
systems.faultCurrent: low (soil path, typically tens of amperes)
systems.primaryProtection: RCD is mandatory (overcurrent will not clear an earth fault)
systems.openPenRisk: none from a utility PEN (there is no utility PE). Local electrode resistance must stay low enough for the RCD.
evNotes: Very common for dwellings in France, Italy, Spain, Japan, much of Africa and South Asia.
A 30 mA RCD on each connecting point is already required by IEC 60364-7-722; TT relies on it for all earth-fault disconnection.
Sometimes used as a local island for an EV circuit on an otherwise TN-C-S (PME) supply — only if the electrode is sufficiently independent of buried bonded metalwork.

systems.name: IT
systems.fullName: Isolé Terre — isolated or impedance-earthed source
systems.installationEarth: local electrodes; first fault does not complete a metallic loop
systems.conductors: typically 3 phases, often no distributed neutral; PE local
systems.faultCurrent: very small on first fault (mA); second fault behaves like TN/TT
systems.primaryProtection: insulation monitoring device (IMD) + alarm on first fault; overcurrent / RCD on second fault
systems.openPenRisk: not applicable (no PEN). First-fault voltage displacement is the issue.
evNotes: Dominant in ~70 % of Norwegian LV networks (230 V line-to-line, no neutral).
Many onboard chargers expect 230 V L–N / 400 V L–L (TN wye). On 230 V IT they only use two lines (single-phase 230 V).
Some vehicles (e.g. certain Tesla models) can use 230 V three-phase IT and reach ~11 kW; others must not be charged three-phase on IT.
IEC 60364-7-722 and vehicle OEM instructions must both be checked before 3-phase IT charging.

iec60364_7_722: No PEN conductor on the EV circuit.
Each AC connecting point: RCD IΔn ≤ 30 mA disconnecting all live conductors.
DC residual protection: RCD Type B, or Type A/F plus RDC-DD (IEC 62955) detecting 6 mA smooth DC.
Protective measures 'non-conducting location' and 'earth-free local bonding' shall not be used.
